at_the_bound.name: control_sync_result_at_262144_bytes
at_the_bound.note: exactly the bound: a page of one record that is a string of 'x' (not a record: it doesn't parse, the page standing); the one byte longer text is control_sync_result_over_262144_bytes

at_the_bound.name: membership_fetch_result_at_262144_bytes
at_the_bound.note: exactly the bound, the same bound as every other relay message (no 512 KiB exemption: only stage 3's mailbox calls get that): one entry of log L (E4) whose signature is padded with 'A', so it is read as a message but its signature would not verify; the one byte longer text is membership_fetch_result_over_262144_bytes

calls.name: control_sync_with_feed_id
calls.note: the host knows the feed: read it after position 2, the last it read

calls.name: control_sync_without_feed_id
calls.note: the host doesn't know the feed yet: no feed_id, and a cursor belongs to a feed, so after is 0

calls.name: control_sync_at_the_largest_position
calls.note: after at 2^53 - 1, the largest integer

calls.name: control_sync_result_empty_feed
calls.note: a feed with no record: head 0, no records

calls.name: control_sync_result_with_records
calls.note: three records of the control vectors, ascending, the last at the head

calls.name: control_sync_result_with_records_that_do_not_parse
calls.note: a page is read whole and each record judged on its own: one with an unknown field, a string and a null don't parse, and the page, the feed's position and the records after them stand (gaps in the positions are allowed)

calls.name: heads_two_stations
calls.note: two feeds, each of another Station, and the device list's head (log L's)

calls.name: heads_without_feeds
calls.note: no feed covers a principal with work on this host: only the device list's head

calls.name: heads_64_feeds
calls.note: the most feeds one heads announces: 64, each once

calls.name: control_ack_cursor_only
calls.note: the host read the feed to position 5 and has applied nothing to report: the cursor says only how far it read

calls.name: control_ack_record_results
calls.note: results of the reset feed's snapshot, by record_id, each with the effect its record carries: a cover applied, a hold pending, a release refused

calls.name: control_ack_revoke_results
calls.note: a revoke (its revocation), a revoke with interrupt_running (revocation already in force, interrupt applied) and a later interrupt_running (its interrupt)

calls.name: control_ack_entry_result
calls.note: the result of a host sender's device-list revoke, by {seq, entry_hash}: applied once applied_seq has reached its seq

calls.name: control_ack_entry_pending
calls.note: the same entry while the host's applied device-list seq is behind it: only pending or refused may be said

calls.name: control_ack_both_result_forms
calls.note: both result forms in one ack: a record's and an entry's (a host sender's revoke that asked for an interrupt: revocation and interrupt)

calls.name: control_ack_64_results
calls.note: the most results one ack carries: 64, each record once (ids of no vectors record)

calls.name: control_ack_with_reasons
calls.note: partial effects with typed reasons (O5): each effect pending or refused says why, a code of the shared why vocabulary (a release issued before the hold in force, an interrupt waiting for its revocation, a stop signed by a removed manager on both its effects, a release that may be an evicted one replayed, a principal the list doesn't hold yet, an entry host-work hasn't applied); the effects in force beside them say nothing. A reason never changes a result and counts nothing

calls.name: control_ack_with_unrecognized_reasons
calls.note: reasons this reader doesn't know (a later version's), one at the 64-byte bound: well formed (1 to 64 bytes of [a-z0-9_]), so read as unrecognized, information only; each result is unchanged and the reason is written back as it came

calls.name: membership_fetch
calls.note: the host holds the device list to seq 2

calls.name: membership_fetch_result
calls.note: the entries after seq 2 (log L's E3 to E6, an R9.3 carriage) and the Station's head; no echo of after, no more

calls.name: membership_fetch_result_no_entries
calls.note: the host is current: the head and no entries

calls.name: control_sync_refused
calls.note: the Station refuses the call on this link (agreed with Astation, 2026-11-11): exactly this, naming nothing

calls.name: membership_fetch_refused
calls.note: the Station refuses the call on this link (agreed with Astation, 2026-11-11): exactly this, naming nothing

calls.name: control_ack_refused
calls.note: the Station refuses the call on this link (agreed with Astation, 2026-11-11): exactly this, naming nothing

name: r9-vectors-station-calls
note: The six Station calls (control_sync, control_sync_result, heads, control_ack, membership_fetch, membership_fetch_result) and the three refusals (control_sync_refused, membership_fetch_refused, control_ack_refused) of host-work-v1 §11.4, as the shared core's own builders write them (planned; nothing advertises them). `calls`: each valid message `{name, op, direction, note, fields, wire, judged?, hand_assembled?}`. `wire` is the exact text: compact, keys in RFC 8785 order (the builders' order), no whitespace; `direction` says who reads it (`to_station`: a host's call, `to_host`: a Station's message; the other reader refuses it as another message); `fields` are what it decodes to (an absent optional field is absent; every value as sent, a page's record as a value). `judged`, for a page: the control parser's verdict on each record, parallel to the records (`parses` with the `record_id`, or not with its parse `error`): a record the parser refuses never costs the page, the feed's position or the records after it. A Station builder can't write such a record (a Station serves only what it stored), so that page's text is a builder's page with the records put in their slots and its case says `hand_assembled: true`: a Station builder given its `fields` refuses it, with the parse code of the first record the parser refuses (that a null or a string record is a record the parser refuses, and the page stands, is Atem's reading of "any JSON type", agreed with Astation on 2026-11-13, #120 comment 6848326392: a strict-JSON page may hold individually invalid records, whose evidence is kept, which aren't applied, and whose delivery is no application evidence). `at_the_bound`: valid texts of exactly `max_message_bytes` bytes, as `wire_fill` recipes `{name, op, direction, note, wire_fill, accepts}` (`accepts`: what the reader gives back: the head, the number of records or entries and, for a page, whether each record parses: `records_parse`), one for each call that can carry a large page (a page's record, a fetch result's entry): the bound is the same for both, `membership_fetch_result` included. `invalid`: texts a reader refuses `{name, op, reader, code, wire}` with the code it gives (`too_large`, `not_strict`, `wrong_message`, `unknown_field` or `malformed`); each has one fault (a text with two is refused by whichever the reader reaches first: the size bound, the strict parse, the message and its op, unknown fields, then the fields' values); `wire_fill` stands for a text of `bytes` bytes written as `prefix`, `count` times `fill`, then `suffix`; the over-the-bound texts of both large-page calls are 262,145 and 300,000 bytes. `max_message_bytes` is R9.9's bound for every relay message, in bytes as sent, checked before any parse. `why_codes` is the shared vocabulary of typed reasons (O5, host-work-v1 §11.4 wire rule 10, for Astation's sign-off), in the core's order: a well-formed reason outside it is a later version's, read as unrecognized. Every valid text is strict I-JSON; `scripts/check-r9-vectors.py` reads every text, valid and invalid, with a reader written from the spec.
